name: CR-V3

codes.note: Listed with 5047LC on the Energizer sheet as 5047LC/LF

dimensions.note: Width is the long side of the two-lobed top view, about the width of two AA cells side by side. The datasheet drawing also shows 14.0 to 14.6 mm and 6.4 to 7.7 mm dimensions on the end-face contacts.

geometry.note: Two AA-sized cylindrical cells side by side in one keyed wrap. The contacts are on one end face: two round recessed holes with the + contact marked on the left lobe, per the datasheet drawing.

variants.notes: Energizer labels the chemical system "Non-Aqueous Lithium" and does not name it. The lithium-manganese-dioxide assignment is inferred from the 3.0 V nominal voltage of the two parallel cells. Wikipedia reports a Duracell CR-V3 made of two 3 V AA-sized lithium cells in parallel.

variants.label: Rechargeable (RCR-V3)
variants.notes: Wikipedia gives a 3.7 V nominal voltage in the CR-V3 article and 3.6 V in the battery size list, and 1,300 mAh without test conditions. Some packs add a small third terminal for charging.

interchange.note: The 2CR5 is a 6 V pack with a different shape and contacts, and it does not fit a CR-V3 compartment.

safety: Lithium photo batteries are single-use and are not designed to be recharged; charging can cause venting, fire or rupture.
Do not short-circuit, crush, heat or disassemble. The battery contains a positive temperature coefficient (PTC) device to limit short-circuit current, but it does not make the battery safe to abuse.
Replace all batteries in a device at the same time and do not mix them with used batteries or other types.
The rechargeable RCR-V3 runs at 3.7 V and charges to a higher voltage; use it only in devices that allow it.
notes: Digital cameras designed for two AA cells or one CR-V3 accept both, and some cameras not designed for it also accept it, per Wikipedia.
